title: Designed to be forgotten
text: Airports are among the few buildings designed to stop you {{1}} what time it is. Nothing about them is accidental. The walk from security to the gate is long partly to {{2}} you through the shops, since passengers who have just surrendered their liquids are proven {{3}}; lighting is even and windowless near the retail to blur the hour; departure boards {{4}} delays quietly, folding bad news into neutral colours. Queues are engineered for {{5}}: a single winding line feels fairer and shorter than several parallel ones, even when the wait is identical, and visible progress — moving every minute — matters more to calm than the {{6}} wait itself. Airlines, meanwhile, have learned that the journey is judged by its {{7}} moments: the moment of boarding, the moment of landing, and the moment the bag arrives. Investment therefore {{8}} there. The airport is not a building but a machine for managing mood, and every surface of it has been tested by people who know exactly what a stressed traveller will pay for a sandwich.

gaps.explanation: 'stop you knowing what time it is' — 'stop someone' takes the gerund; knowledge and knack are nouns.
'to funnel you through the shops' — steer through a narrow route, like a funnel; furnish = equip.
'proven spenders' — people who spend money; spinner = someone or something that spins.
'departure boards announce delays quietly' — display them publicly; denounce = condemn, renounce = give up a claim.
'engineered for calm' — the noun is needed after 'for'; calming is the adjective and calmly the adverb.
'matters more than the actual wait' — the real one, contrasted with how it feels; virtual = simulated.
'the journey is judged by its peak moments' — the highs and lows; judging by averages or totals is exactly what the passage rules out, and pique is wounded pride.
'investment pours there' — flows abundantly; pore = study closely (pore over), paw = touch clumsily.
